newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -Dlr/mark vols up as spot continues climb.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -Dlr/mark vols up as spot continues climb.

text.p: Dollar/mark option volatilities were bid higher in busy European trade, following dollar spot's climb to its highest levels since October 1989.
The dollar's test of levels around 1.88 marks kept up the recent demand for dollar calls, particularly in the longer-dated options with strikes in the 2.00 marks region.
"Dollar/mark vols are looking expensive so these low delta plays make a lot of sense now. They're relatively cheap and if you get it right, the leverage is huge," said a U.S. bank options dealer.

One-month dollar/mark volatility stood at 11.0/11.4 percent at midday Europe, up from 10.6/11.0 late Monday. Further out, one-year vols were also modestly firmer at 11.0/11.2 percent from 10.8/11.2 Monday.
The dollar/mark risk reversal, the difference in implied volatility of calls relative to puts, was static at 0.5/0.7 percent for mark puts.

Dollar/mark spot made a fairly muted European start but found its legs in morning trade after the Bundesbank opted to refrain from engineering higher money-market rates at today's German repo tender to defend its currency.
Dollar/yen volatilities were steady as the spot rate kept within its recent 118-119 yen range.
Dealers said the technical resistance at 119 was still holding dollar/yen back as was mark/yen weakness but good demand for yen puts, particularly at the 120 strike, was keeping vols underpinned.
One-month dollar/yen vol stood at 11.45/11.60 percent against 11.4/11.7 Monday. The risk reversal was steady at 0.3/0.6 percent for yen puts.

Sterling/mark, meantime, was higher with dollar/mark but option vols were largely steady in cautious trade ahead of this week's Bank of England monetary policy committee meeting. Expectations of a UK interest rate hike at Thursday's meeting are still running high, putting the risk to the downside if the Bank of England holds steady, said dealers.
"Vols are pretty subdued at the moment, people don't really want to lean very far in any direction ahead of Thursday," said a UK bank dealer.
One-month sterling/mark stood at 10.5/10.8 percent from 10.6/10.9 late Monday. The risk reversal edged in favour of sterling calls from trading around par.
